lead.headline: Iran, Oman agree on Hormuz route as US presses for deal
lead.dek: The waterway, shut since late February, normally carries a fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas.
body: Iran and Oman have agreed on coordinates for a commercial shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said Wednesday. A joint statement covering technical, legal, security and environmental terms is under final review.

The strait, which carried about a fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas, has been effectively closed since Iran shut it after U.S. and Israeli strikes in late February. Under the proposal, ships would enter the Gulf through an Iranian-controlled lane and exit through an Omani one.

Tehran wants service fees for security and environmental protection. Washington refuses. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said talks had progressed but had not reached finality. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said a deal could come within a day or two.

briefs.headline: Senate confirms Erica Schwartz as CDC director, 51-44
briefs.summary: Schwartz, a retired rear admiral and former deputy surgeon general, fills a post vacant since Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. fired Susan Monarez last August.

briefs.headline: Wyden report says banks ignored Epstein red flags
briefs.summary: A Senate Finance report, “Looking the Other Way,” says Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and JPMorgan Chase left suspicious transfers unreported to Treasury for nearly two decades.

briefs.headline: Experts question FDA’s ‘lower risk’ label on Zyn pouches
briefs.summary: The FDA cleared 20 Zyn nicotine pouch products to claim lower cancer and heart risk than cigarettes. Lifetime use among 12th graders rose to 10% from 6.8%.

briefs.headline: Russian barrage kills 17 in Kyiv and surrounding region
briefs.summary: Russia fired 24 ballistic missiles and 115 drones overnight Wednesday. Ukraine downed none of the missiles, and Zelenskyy blamed a Patriot interceptor shortage.

briefs.headline: Congo Ebola deaths pass 1,700 as WHO speeds up drug trials
briefs.summary: The Bundibugyo strain has killed 1,707 people among 3,802 cases since May 15. Ituri province accounts for nearly 90 percent of infections.

briefs.headline: US revokes visa of Brazil’s ambassador in envoy standoff
briefs.summary: The State Department pulled Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti’s visa Tuesday after Brazil stalled the U.S. nominee. She was not expelled.

briefs.headline: Trump OKs $4.5M in flood aid for Upshur, Lewis counties
briefs.summary: Federal Individual Assistance was approved after the July 21 flooding. FEMA is still weighing disaster requests from five other West Virginia counties.

briefs.headline: Greenbrier’s $500M deal on track, big hurdles remain
briefs.summary: Lawyers say the Kennedy Lewis financing should close by Aug. 7, but a debtholder payoff and Lottery Commission approval of the casino license are unsettled.

regional.item: Cabell County’s school board approved baseball, softball and co-ed soccer at all four middle schools, starting in spring 2027.
New bleachers, a press box and accessible walkways are going in at Poca High School’s O.O. White Stadium ahead of the Aug. 28 home opener.
Parkersburg hosts an Aug. 13 town hall on independent testing results from the Peoples Cartage warehouse fire.
Elliott Pritt, the District 50 House candidate from Fayette County, quit the November ballot after a federal child-enticement arrest.

away.item: Bennington received the remains of Army Pfc. Bernard Sweet, who died in a Japanese POW camp in 1942 and was identified by DNA last year.
Prince George Coun. Frizzell entered the mayor’s race, pitching economic development and public safety as his priorities.
A nonprofit led by Pender County Commissioner Jimmy Tate is under state review over complaints alleging Medicaid fraud.

fishing.line: Down to 108 cfs from 251 yesterday, 1.68 ft and falling — prime wading water.
Ocean highs 12:14 AM and 1:02 PM; water 83.3F at Wrightsville Beach, 25 mi up the coast.

briefs.headline: West Virginia opens fall camp, quarterback job unsettled
briefs.summary: The Mountaineers held their first practice Wednesday. Rich Rodriguez has not named a starter between Scotty Fox Jr. and Oklahoma transfer Michael Hawkins Jr.

briefs.headline: Sumo association doubles top-division championship purse
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association will raise the makuuchi title prize to 20 million yen in January 2027, its first purse revision since 1994. Salaries also rise.

briefs.headline: Bears, tackle Darnell Wright agree to record $116M deal
briefs.summary: The four-year extension includes $93 million guaranteed, the most ever for an NFL offensive lineman. Wright becomes the highest-paid right tackle at $29 million a year.

briefs.headline: COVID reactivates dormant viruses in half of severe cases
briefs.summary: A Nature study of more than 1,100 hospitalized patients found nearly half reactivated latent viruses such as Epstein-Barr, tracking with longer stays and death.

briefs.headline: NHTSA opens probe into 1.2 million Tesla Model 3s and Ys
briefs.summary: Regulators are investigating 156 complaints that a front lower lateral link detaches without warning on 2018-2020 Model 3s and 2021-2023 Model Ys.

briefs.headline: Climate change made Spanish fire weather 20 times likelier
briefs.summary: World Weather Attribution found human warming made July’s extreme fire conditions at least 20 times more likely in central Spain and twice as likely in southwest France.
